Premium Hepa Air Filtration (Bypass) Installation to existing Ductwork High Efficiency Particulate Arrestance (HEPA) filters are used in hospitals because they are considered the best filters on the market today. HEPA filters were originally developed by the Atomic Energy Commission during World War II to remove hazardous radioactive dust from manufacturing plant exhausts. In order to receive a HEPA filter designation, a filter must collect 99.97% of a specific particulate that measures 0.3 microns in size, in tests established by the Institute of Environmental Sciences. The Pristine Air HEPA system is 99.97% at .3 microns and removes particles as small as .01 microns. HEPA systems usually require a significant amount of fan energy to force air through the filtration media. The PAHP-300 system overcomes this requirement by positioning the system parallel to, instead of across, the airstream. Polluted air is directed through the filter on multiple passes to cleanse the air. Working in combination with a pre-filter to capture larger particles, the system is designed to operate at peak performance for up to two years before requiring replacement of the HEPA filters
  • HEPA filter should be replaced every two years.

️ How the LXDAN System Works
  1. Untreated water enters the mineral tank and moves through neutralizing media.
  2. Media dissolves into the water, raising pH and correcting corrosive acidity.
  3. Treated water exits the system free of corrosive properties that damage copper piping and fixtures.
  4. The system automatically schedules backwash cycles to clean, lift, and reset the media bed, ensuring continued pH correction.
    • Over time, additional media must be added as part of normal consumption.

Lancaster Plumbing Heating Cooling Electrical will contact appropriate utilities before excavation to mark gas, electric, and communication lines. On the day of installation, technicians will excavate using an excavator to dig a trench for the sewer line. A section of the existing line may be removed (if needed) and new code-compliant piping will be installed. Pipe will be bedded with stone above and below. A new clean-out and/or house trap will be installed as required by code. The new line will be pitched for proper drainage. The trench will be backfilled and tamped as work proceeds, and finish will be a rough grade only.


LPHCE does not provide grass seed, shrubs, or landscaping. These are the responsibility of the homeowner and not included in our scope. Settling may occur. While we make every reasonable attempt to back fill, it is the homeowner’s responsibility to address future settling.
Excavation may uncover obstructions, objects, or roots. Roots may cause landscaping damage despite our efforts to prevent it. This is outside our control, and we cannot be held liable.
Rocks may be present and topsoil may need to be added at the homeowner's expense. Concrete, fence reinstall, grass seeding, straw, or any landscaping is NOT included and is the homeowner’s responsibility.
Municipalities may restrict replacement from Nov 1 – Apr 1 if the job involves sidewalk or asphalt street work. We will coordinate a return visit for replacement if needed.
Underground Dog Fence: We cannot avoid or protect underground dog fences. If excavation is needed near one, it is likely to be damaged. Repairs will be the homeowner’s responsibility.
Buried Items: Tanks, wells, septic systems, or excessive rocks cannot be guaranteed to be avoided. If discovered, we will work to minimize cost, but all related expenses (e.g., rock clearing, drilling, tank removal, sinkhole repair) will be passed to the customer.
Warranty: Full sewer line replacements from home to curb or municipal main using Schedule 40 PVC are backed by our Exclusive Lifetime Warranty.
If utility markings reveal interference with the proposed line path, we will quickly propose a new safety plan and work scope for approval.
Use of excavation equipment may cause wear to driveways, grass, or landscaping. We take reasonable steps to minimize damage but are not responsible for property damage from standard work procedures.
* Lifetime Warranty applies to the original purchaser only, must be Schedule 40 PVC, and run from foundation to the main municipal sewer. Does not cover backups due to misuse (e.g., grease or wipes). Standard charges apply.

*** Schedule 35 SDR complete replacements include a 10-year warranty. Pipe material is dictated by local code.
**** Abandoned tanks, wells, or cavities uncovered during excavation will be addressed case-by-case. Municipal codes often require filling with stone at the homeowner's expense.
***** Permits or municipal requirements may arise unexpectedly. Homeowners will be advised of any associated costs.
****** LPHCE is not liable for damage caused by natural disasters or events beyond normal use.

The straight facts Under ideal conditions, like when the A/C coils are clean, the system operates at peak efficiency. However, multiple factors can lead to decreased operating efficiency and higher energy costs. Dirt buildup is perhaps the coils' number one enemy. Dirt prohibits the proper transfer of heat over the coils, acting as an insulation of sorts that prevents heat from moving through the coils as it should. Dirty coils show a direct correlation to a lower system cooling capacity, in worst-case scenarios delivering a 30 percent reduction in capacity. This happens because dirt resting on coils increases the total pressure within the system when it's operating, and it increases operating temperatures, too. Premium Hepa Air Filtration (Bypass) Installation to existing Ductwork in a remote mount application High-Efficiency Particulate Arrestance (HEPA) filters are used in hospitals because they are considered the best filters on the market today. HEPA filters were originally developed by the Atomic Energy Commission during World War II to remove hazardous radioactive dust from manufacturing plant exhausts. In order to receive a HEPA filter designation, a filter must collect 99.97% of a specific particulate that measures 0.3 microns in size, in tests established by the Institute of Environmental Sciences. The Pristine Air HEPA system is 99.97% at .3 microns and removes particles as small as .01 microns. HEPA systems usually require a significant amount of fan energy to force air through the filtration media. The PAHP-300 system overcomes this requirement by positioning the system parallel to, instead of across, the airstream. Polluted air is directed through the filter on multiple passes to cleanse the air. Working in combination with a pre-filter to capture larger particles, the system is designed to operate at peak performance for up to two years before requiring replacement of the HEPA filters
  • HEPA filter should be replaced every two years
  • Pre-filter should be replaced every 6 months

  • According to howstuffworks.com :
Dirt is the biggest enemy of your furnace. It can waste fuel and drastically lower efficiency. Dirt affects all three basic components of your furnace, so cleaning is the most important part of regular maintenance. Clean blower assembly, belts and pulleys to blower, and motor housing. Cleaning blower is critical if furnace has a squirrel-cage fan, because openings in this type of blower often become clogged with dirt.
  • According to Angie's List :

The straight facts

Under ideal conditions, like when the A/C coils are clean, the system operates at peak efficiency. However, multiple factors can lead to decreased operating efficiency and higher energy costs. Dirt buildup is perhaps the coils' number one enemy. Dirt prohibits the proper transfer of heat over the coils, acting as an insulation of sorts that prevents heat from moving through the coils as it should. Some experts estimate that dirty coils consume as much as 37 percent more energy than coils that are clean. Energy costs are not the only result of inefficient coils. Dirty coils show a direct correlation to a lower system cooling capacity, in worst-case scenarios delivering a 30 percent reduction in capacity. This happens because dirt resting on coils increases the total pressure within the system when it's operating, and it increases operating temperatures, too. Over time, these conditions compromise the lubricant on the compressor, causing a costly system failure. ****** Coupons not accepted on this task

The straight facts Under ideal conditions, like when the A/C coils are clean, the system operates at peak efficiency. Dirt prohibits the proper transfer of heat over the coils, acting as an insulation of sorts that prevents heat from moving through the coils as it should. Custom Sewer Solution Lancaster Plumbing Heating Cooling Electrical or the designated subcontractor shall contact appropriate utilities prior to excavation to mark the following items as needed: gas, electric, and communications lines. Starting in basement, jackhammer floor to gain access to sewer lateral. Cut out section of sewer lateral to begin setting up for pipe burst. Outside home, excavate down to gain access to sewer house trap. Cut out and remove house trap. Once trap is removed, begin process of pipe bursting. This is achieved by running steel cable through existing sewer line to both access points inside and outside. Large steel, compression burst head is then attached to the steel cable. Compression side of the pipe is then attached to high density polyethylene pipe. Hydraulic pipe bursting equipment will then be setup at one of the access points. As the pipe bursting equipment pulls the new HDPE pipe through the existing sewer line, the large compression burst head splits the old pipe out of the way and allows the new pipe to then come in behind it. Once work has been completed and pipe pulled completely through lateral, pipe bursting equipment is removed and final connections are made on either end to the existing sewer latera. Both access points are then restored to rough grade, with final flooring inside and final landscaping outside being the responsibility of the customer. Premium Hepa Air Filtration (Bypass) Installation ON existing Ductwork High-efficiency particulate Arrestance (HEPA) filters are used in hospitals because they are considered the best filters on the market today. HEPA filters were originally developed by the Atomic Energy Commission during World War II to remove hazardous radioactive dust from manufacturing plant exhausts. In order to receive a HEPA filter designation, a filter must collect 99.97% of a specific particulate that measures 0.3 microns in size, in tests established by the Institute of Environmental Sciences. The Pristine Air HEPA system is 99.97% at .3 microns and removes particles as small as .01 microns. HEPA systems usually require a significant amount of fan energy to force air through the filtration media. The PAHP-300 system overcomes this requirement by positioning the system parallel to, instead of across, the airstream. Polluted air is directed through the filter on multiple passes to cleanse the air. Working in combination with a pre-filter to capture larger particles, the system is designed to operate at peak performance for up to two years before requiring replacement of the HEPA filters
  • HEPA filter should be replaced every two years
  • Pre-filter should be replaced every 6 months

Ground and Neutral separation for main/ sub panels

Ground and Neutral Separation – Main Panels and Subpanels When a panel is no longer the first means of disconnect, such as when the main disconnect is located outside the home, the neutral and ground must be separated in that panel.
  • Main Service Panel: The neutral and ground are bonded together at the service disconnect, where permitted by the applicable code.
  • Subpanel: The neutral bar must be isolated from the panel enclosure, and the ground bar must be bonded to the enclosure. Neutrals and grounds must terminate on their respective bars and remain separate.
Code Compliance: Proper neutral and ground separation helps prevent normal neutral current from flowing on grounding conductors and metal enclosures.
